title: GM 4.3 / 5.3 / 6.2 / 6.6 gas: shudder or surge at steady speed from a sticking camshaft actuator magnet
summary: GM bulletin 22-NA-080: an engine-side shudder or surge at steady speed that's easy to mistake for the transmission. Watch Camshaft Position Variance in GDS2; over 3-4 degrees while it's happening points at the cam actuator magnet.

specs.name: Camshaft Position Variance, normal
specs.value: Target 0 degrees; up to 3-4 degrees is not unusual on a good system

specs.name: Suspect
specs.value: Variance over 3-4 degrees while the shudder or surge is happening

steps.text: Rule out the transmission first. Customers often describe this as a transmission shudder or surge at steady speed.
Reproduce the shudder while watching "Camshaft Position Variance" in GDS2.
If variance goes past 3-4 degrees during the event and the problem is isolated to the cam actuator system, replace the camshaft actuator magnet and re-evaluate.
If it still shudders with variance over 4 degrees after the magnet, go back to GM service information for further diagnosis.

body: Replaces PIP5794B. The bulletin's vehicle table (models, year ranges and engines) does not extract cleanly from the PDF, so the ranges here are its outer bounds; confirm the engine RPO against page 1 of the bulletin.
